summary: "Zur Psychopathologie des Alltagslebens" by Sigmund Freud is a work published in 1901. The founder of psychoanalysis examines the hidden meanings behind everyday mistakes, slips of the tongue, and forgotten names. Freud argues these seemingly random errors reveal unconscious thoughts and impulses, blurring the line between normal and abnormal psychology.
